txt: Her nose is already back in her magazine. "Uh-huh."

She looks up from her magazine, eyes filled with tired ennui.
She looks up from under her brow.
She pops her raspberry-flavoured bubblegum and nods.
She scrunches up her face into an expression of consummate adolescent scepticism.
She's playing with her hair, engrossed in a magazine.
The clerk stares at you, but doesn't say a thing for a moment or two.
"... Huh? Speed, like... *speed* speed? No, Frittte doesn't do that..." She blinks at you, bewildered.

"Fucking with Frittte is *dangerous*, you know." She scratches her cheek, thinking. "Just leave it there, I'll put it away later."
"Here you go, mister."
"Here you go." The clerk removes the garment from the lower shelf and hands it over.
"Hey, you can't smoke in here." The girl's voice betrays little interest or enthusiasm. She doesn't even look up when as she continues: "Please don't fuck with Frittte."

"I don't know -- Frittte?" She shrugs.
"I don't know, look at the clock. It's right behind you on the wall."
"I don't know. Really *long*?"
"I don't know. What about it?"
"I don't really know anything? I mean, I'm fifteen."
"I don't really know what Hypnogamma is. I guess it makes you feel less shit? It's recommended to use after lots of partying, studying, or exercising."
"I dunno." She shrugs. "It stops people from robbing Frittte, I guess? If they know there's an army, I mean... I wouldn't want to fuck with them, anyway."
"I mean, I already said it'd hurt you? I don't know what else they do." She stares at  you, unsure.
"I mean, I didn't just see a middle-aged man try to steal a four reál raincoat, did I?"
"I mean, it doesn't even cost that much... like, why would you want to 'fuck with Frittte' over something like this?"
"I mean, science is doing great... and this radiocomputer thing seems to be kinda big? I don't know." She shrugs, then folds her magazine back.
"I think science still doesn't know? There's only speculation."
"I think they think that extra T makes it *funkier*..." She chews on her gum with disgust. "It doesn't."
"I'm obliged to inform you that both alcohol and cigarettes damage your health," she comments as you eye the goods behind her, "but I guess you already know that."
"I'm obliged to inform you that both alcohol and cigarettes damage your health. But I guess you already know that."

"In a good place?"  She rubs her face, thinking.

"M'kay..." She returns to her magazine.
"M'kay." She hands you a small capsule. "Don't, like... over-do it or something."
"M'kay." She scratches her nose.
"M'kay." She's chewing on her bubblegum again. "What do you want to know?"
"Mh." She looks down, back into her magazine.
"Mhmh, right behind you." She nods towards the buzzing machine in the corner.
"Mkay, here. I hope Saint-Batiste makes you feel better or something."
"No, I don't think so."
"No." She doesn't even bother looking up out of her magazine. "You need tare to use the tare machine."
"No." She fixes her hair underneath her cap. "Frittte only sells legal drugs, like the law says."
"Not really?"
"Not that they would know anything about being high, it's just an expression." The girl adjusts her hat.
"Or do you mean something else...? Sorry, I really need to finish this article." She taps the magazine on the counter.
"Our government?"
"Reality? You mean... what reality? Economic reality? Or..."
"Saint-Batiste Pharmaceuticals? The one that sells meds out of Saint-Batiste?" She points to the cabinet. "That one? There?"
"Saint-Batiste? You know..." She nods slowly at the cabinet. "The pharmaceuticals company?"
"Sure." She tilts her head back at the shelf. "So... are you going to buy anything, or...?"
"That wasn't very hard." She folds her magazine back.
"This is Pop-Stars, it's got, like, famous people in it? It's not for sale."
"Though some of my friends from school have actually *travelled* through pale on their trip to Mundi. They said it was like being high." She smiles widely, then catches herself.
"Uh, wow, I didn't know you worked for the Union, sir." She rolls up the giant novelty cheque -- looks like she's seen it before -- and slips it under the counter.
"Uh-uh." She brushes a strand of hair off her face and tries to return to her magazine.
"Uhm, I don't really know anything? I mean, I know it's there? But I haven't seen it, so..."
"Uhm, it's where they rate different outfits famous people wear? It's kinda funny. They're kinda mean." She stops to think. "It's about who's the most stylish."
"Uhm, just ask me if you need anything from Saint-Batiste. We don't stock prescription meds, but we do have nosaphed, drouamine, magnesium and hypnogamma."
"Uhm, no. I didn't know him at all."
"Uhm, no. I don't like it, I hate it."
"Uhm, okay..." she looks at the fridge. "It wouldn't even fit you know."
"Uhm, we're in a.... we're in a..." She rubs her face, thinking.
"Uhm, you kicked the tare machine. Please don't kick the tare machine. This is Frittte -- and you don't want to fuck with Frittte."
"Uhm... I don't know, let's see... Nosaphed is a nasal spray. Drouamine is a really good painkiller. Magnesium is a dietary supplement. Hypnogamma is..." She stops.
"Uhm... I don't know?"
"Uhm..." Her lazy eyes scan up and down your body, assessing the situation.
"Uhm..." She chews her bubblegum absent-mindedly. "No, sorry. I'm not, like, a doctor or anything."
"Uhm..." She keeps chewing on her gum. "You're joking, right?"
"Uhm..." She looks up from her magazine, not really sure how to reply.
"Um, did you..." The girl stares at the package lying on the floor. It looks a little sad as it lies in the dusty floor.
"Um, is this about the questions again? 'Cause I don't really know anything..." She puts down the magazine.
"Um, okay. I'm not really supposed to be chatting to anyone, but..." She puts down the magazine.

"Um... Guess not, no." She looks at the wall of goods behind her, then adjusts her hat.
"Um... Sure. If you want something, I can get it for you. Just let me know and pay and stuff..." She adjusts her hat.
"We're in Frittte?"
"We're in Revachol? Like, on the Insulindian isola?"
"We're in a *transition*! You know, transitioning from, uh... monarchy to democracy, all that stuff." She nods, then folds her magazine back.
"Welcome to Frittte! Feel free to look around or something, everything is out on the shelves." She returns to her magazine.

"Yeah, it happened like 50 years ago or so. Sorry, I'm not very good at this. At history, I mean."
"Yeah, like two thousand or so." She says it as if it's completely natural.
"Yeah, me neither."
"Yeah, super funny." She returns to her magazine, seemingly not impressed by the joke.
"Yeah, they're kind of boring, but, you know..." She never finishes the sentence.
"Yeah... there's like an ampoule somewhere." She waves her hand in the air absent-mindedly.
"Yeah..." She's not really paying attention to you anymore.
"Yeah." She looks at the clock on the wall. "That's why I'm working my ass off in Frittte. So I guess, like, that's economic."
"Yes -- buy it, please, don't steal it..." The clerk removes the garment from the dusty floor and hands it over.
"Yes." She hitches her thumb toward the end of the counter. "What we have is there, in the medicine cabinet -- go take a look yourself..."
"You know..." She shrugs, uninterested in explaining it further.
"You mean this?" She looks at the cover boasting a colourful photo of two girls kissing.
"You need a bag I guess? We used to have some but we gave them all out, so..." She shrugs awkwardly.
"You think the police, like... bother catching shoplifters?" She rolls her eyes. "Frittte polices themselves, so... Yeah. Anything else you wanted?"
"You're welcome?" She folds her magazine back.
